faq_search_title: How do I search for a sample?
faq_search_step_words: Type a few words in the search bar on the home page, such as a sample name or an IGSN, then press “Search”.
faq_search_step_location: Looking for samples from a region? Click “Add location”, then “Draw an area” and click two opposite corners on the map (or hold Shift and drag). You can search by words, by area, or both.
faq_search_step_filters: On the results page, use the filters to narrow things down by type, material, age, collector and more. Remove a filter from its chip, or start over with “Clear all filters”.
faq_search_step_map: Click “See on map” to see where your results were collected, and open any result to see its full description.
faq_search_rules_title: How does the search find samples?
faq_search_rule_fields: It looks in each sample’s name, specific name and local name, and finds the samples containing all the words you typed. You can also type an IGSN to find that exact sample.
faq_search_rule_case: No need to worry about capitals or accents: “rhone” also finds “Rhône”.
faq_search_rule_typo: Small typos are forgiven in words of 5 letters or more: “basslt” still finds “basalt”.
faq_search_rule_wildcard: Not sure of the spelling? Use the “*” wildcard in place of any letters: “bas*lt” finds “basalt”.
faq_search_rule_phrase: Put words in quotes to find them side by side, in that order: "basalt powder" finds “Basalt powder” but not “Powder of basalt”. Typos are not forgiven inside quotes, and single quotes work too.
faq_search_rule_operators: Type OR (or OU) between two words to find either of them, and AND (or ET) to find both, in capitals. Use parentheses to group them: "(basalt OR granite) powder" finds basalt or granite powders.
faq_search_rule_limits: Keep it short: only the first 6 words or quoted phrases are used, and single letters are skipped.
faq_search_rule_area: When searching by location, draw an area no bigger than a quarter of the globe. A larger area turns red and is not searched.
faq_search_rule_published: Only published samples are shown. Sub-samples are hidden by default: turn on “Include sub-samples” in the filters to see them.
faq_igsn_answer: The IGSN (International Generic Sample Number) is a unique, persistent and resolvable identifier assigned to a physical sample (rock, core, sediment, thin section, powder…). Since the partnership between IGSN e.V. and DataCite, IGSNs are registered as DOIs: they can be cited, linked to data and publications, and tracked throughout the sample’s life cycle (field, laboratories, collections). They help make samples FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable).
faq_application_title: What is the IGSN V2 application for?
faq_application_answer: It lets staff of the Earth and environmental sciences community declare their samples, describe their metadata according to a common model and obtain an IGSN for each one. The service is currently limited to the solid Earth domain (rocks, sediments, minerals, synthetic/experimental materials, as well as extraterrestrial rocks and materials), but is meant to be extended to other sub-domains, notably the Ocean-Atmosphere (OA) and Surface and Intercontinental (SIC) communities. Each IGSN points to a public page (“landing page”) describing the sample.
faq_audience_answer_1: The IGSN-CNRS service is open to all higher education and research staff, whatever their institution or parent organisation. It is aimed in particular at researchers, engineers, technicians, PhD students and research support staff who collect, produce, study or use samples as part of their scientific activities.
faq_audience_answer_2: It can also be used by laboratories, platforms, research infrastructures and facilities that manage or store samples, to make them easier to identify, discover and link with the associated data and scientific resources.
faq_sesar_title: How is it different from SESAR²?
faq_sesar_answer: SESAR² is an IGSN allocating agent operated in the United States, which uses a shared prefix (10.58052). The IGSN V2 application plays the same role for the French community, with a metadata model and vocabularies suited to its thematic domains, and CNRS hosting. Both systems produce IGSNs of the same kind, interoperable through DataCite.
faq_price_answer: No. The IGSN allocation service is funded by its partners (see the list of partners).
faq_sign_in_answer: You sign in with your institution’s credentials through the RENATER identity federation. We strongly recommend linking your ORCID to your profile, so that your samples stay attached to you even if you change institution.
faq_orcid_title: How do I link my ORCID to my IGSN account?
faq_orcid_answer: Once signed in, open your profile and add your “ORCID ID”. You are redirected to the ORCID website to sign in and authorise the application, then you come back to your profile. Your ORCID iD is then shown there. If you do not have an ORCID yet, you can create one for free at https://orcid.org. An IGSN account can only be linked to one ORCID.
faq_sign_in_trouble_title: I can no longer sign in. What should I do?
faq_sign_in_trouble_answer: Sign-in goes through your institution via the RENATER federation, so the application does not manage your password. First check that you chose the right institution in the list and that your credentials work on your institution’s other services. If you have changed institution or your institutional account has been deactivated, contact your institutional manager (lab, OSU) or your space manager. Failing that, contact us: we can attach your samples to your new account, relying in particular on your ORCID.
faq_sharing_title: Can I share the management of my samples with other people?
faq_sharing_answer: Yes. Your samples can be managed within a shared space (team, unit, project…) whose manager grants rights to its members (read, edit, create). For institutional records, this is the recommended method, rather than sharing a generic account.
faq_object_types_title: What kinds of objects can I register?
faq_object_types_answer: Any physical object from the natural environment or from an experiment: individual sample, core, core section, sediment sample, thin section, powder, mineral separate, etc. The object type is chosen from a controlled vocabulary.
faq_required_metadata_title: Which metadata are required to publish a sample?
faq_required_metadata_answer_1: A minimal core is required: sample name, object type, collection date, collector’s first and last name, location, as well as the elements required by DataCite (creator/responsible party, date, publisher). We strongly recommend filling in as much information as possible, in particular the classification (lithology, mineralogy…), the collection method and the current storage location, as these are the most searched fields.
faq_required_metadata_answer_2: The model is based on the “IGSN Sample Core” schema, built with and for the scientific communities concerned. It is aligned with DataCite, OGC OMS, ISO 19115 / ISO 19115-1, iSamples and SKOS/URI.
faq_batch_import_title: Can I register samples in batches?
faq_batch_import_answer: Yes, by importing a tabular file (template provided and configurable online). The application checks the file before registering the samples and reports errors row by row.
faq_reservation_title: Can I pre-reserve internal IDs for my future samples?
faq_reservation_answer: Yes. Pre-reservation generates a batch import file holding internal IDs (SAMPLE-xxxxx). This is particularly useful for field missions or sea campaigns: the metadata can be entered in this file during the mission, or completed afterwards.
faq_igsn_format_title: What does an IGSN assigned by the application look like?
faq_igsn_format_answer: It is a DOI made of a prefix (the service’s) and a random, non-meaningful 26-character suffix, for example 10.xxxxx/01M3RNZ4KNET6TFM24S9XNFQTA. The suffix is deliberately non-meaningful, so as not to encode information (location, parent…) that could become wrong.
faq_own_igsn_title: Can I choose my own IGSN?
faq_own_igsn_answer: By default, the application automatically generates a random identifier (UUID + hashing to limit it to 26 characters), which guarantees its uniqueness. For your internal organisation or readability needs, a “Local Name” field is available; its content is left to the depositors’ discretion.
faq_cannot_publish_title: I cannot publish samples. What should I do?
faq_cannot_publish_item_1: Your account is not validated yet. Until the manager of your space has validated your account and attached it to their space, you can create and edit draft records, but you cannot validate them. The manager is notified when you sign up. If your request goes unanswered, contact them directly.
faq_cannot_publish_item_2: Your role does not allow you to validate the record. Only the record’s creator and the editors they designated can validate it. If you are a contributor, you can view and edit the record, but not validate it. Ask the record’s creator to designate you as an editor.
faq_cannot_publish_item_3: Mandatory metadata are missing. The application blocks validation until the minimal core is filled in (see “Which metadata are required?”). The missing fields are flagged on the record.
faq_cannot_publish_answer_2: Finally, if your record is validated but does not appear publicly yet, check whether it has an embargo date: the metadata only become public on that date (see “Are my metadata public?”).
faq_sub_samples_title: How do I manage a sample and its sub-samples?
faq_sub_samples_answer: A “parent” sample is one from which others (“children”) are derived: fractions, powders, thin sections… Each sub-sample receives its own IGSN and references its parent’s IGSN. Several generations are possible. The relation is not encoded in the identifier, but in the metadata.
faq_sub_samples_item_1: You hold both the parent and the child: register both, and enter the parent’s IGSN in the child’s record.
faq_sub_samples_item_2: You hold only the parent: register it, and share its IGSN with the holders of the sub-samples.
faq_sub_samples_item_3: You hold only the child: register it; if the parent is registered later, you will be able to add the link.
faq_foreign_parent_title: How do I declare a sub-sample of a sample I did not declare?
faq_foreign_parent_answer_1: Declare your sub-sample like any other sample: it receives its own IGSN. The link with the parent sample depends on the parent’s situation.
faq_foreign_parent_item_1: The parent already has an IGSN assigned by our service: enter this IGSN on the sub-sample, in the field for the parent sample. The link will appear on your sub-sample’s public page. You do not need rights on the parent’s record. If the parent has an IGSN assigned by our service, the parent’s creator is automatically notified that a sub-sample has been created.
faq_foreign_parent_item_2: The parent has no IGSN: we recommend asking its holder (colleague, collection, core repository) to declare it, then adding its IGSN to your record. In the meantime, you can describe your sub-sample’s origin in a relation to another identifier (dataset DOI, collection record URL, local identifier…) or in the record’s description. You can add the link to the parent at any time, without your sub-sample’s IGSN changing.
faq_foreign_parent_answer_2: Do not declare a parent sample that you do not hold yourself: its record must be managed by the person or institution responsible for it.
faq_public_metadata_answer: The service is part of an open science approach: we strongly recommend making all metadata available to the community through the publish button. A restricted publication mode is nevertheless available for sensitive samples. An embargo is possible through a deferred publication date; its duration is however limited to 2 years.
faq_editing_title: Can I edit the metadata after registration?
faq_editing_answer: Yes, at any time, individually or in batches. The identifier, however, never changes.
faq_deletion_answer: No. An IGSN is persistent: once published, it must stay resolvable. If a sample is destroyed, lost or used up, its record is kept and its status must be updated. Only records that were never published (drafts) can be deleted. You can however ask the service administrator to deactivate an IGSN (“Tombstone” status), through a dedicated form; you will be asked for a detailed justification.
faq_find_by_igsn_title: How do I find a sample from its IGSN?
faq_find_by_igsn_answer: Type https://doi.org/ followed by the IGSN in a browser, or use the application’s search engine. You land on the sample’s public page.
faq_citation_title: How do I cite an IGSN in a publication?
faq_citation_answer: Give the identifier as a DOI, for example IGSN: 10.xxxxx/01M3RNZ4KNET6TFM24S9XNFQTA or, in full, https://doi.org/10.xxxxx/01M3RNZ4KNET6TFM24S9XNFQTA. Remember to mention it in the associated datasets too (e.g. in a data repository), to link samples, data and articles.
faq_collection_citation_title: How do I cite all the samples I declared, or those of one of my manual groups, in a publication?
faq_collection_citation_answer_1: For your samples, copy the “My sample link” link from your profile. This public link leads to the list of all the samples you have published.
faq_collection_citation_answer_2: For the samples of the manual groups you belong to, copy from your profile the “Group sample link” link of the group whose samples you want. This public link leads to the list of all the samples published in this group.
faq_collection_citation_answer_3: You can cite these links in your article, for example in the “Data availability” or “Samples” section, so that readers reach all your samples and their records in one click (your sub-samples are reachable through their parents).
faq_collection_citation_answer_4: These links evolve with your deposits: they will also show the samples you declare later.
faq_collection_citation_answer_5: Once the article is published, add its DOI to your samples’ records with the “is cited by” (IsCitedBy) relation. This can be done in batches. Your samples will then point to the publication that uses them.
faq_labels_answer: Yes. Each sample record shows a QR code on its public page, which you can copy and print in the size and on the medium of your choice. Prefer a suitable medium (durable labels, glued or set in resin).
faq_api_title: Is there an API to view, declare or edit samples from a third-party application?
faq_api_answer: Yes. An API lets you create, view and update samples from your own tools and business applications (LIMS, collection databases, scripts). It requires authentication. Documentation: https://igsn.insu.fr/api/service/docs
faq_missing_term_title: A term I need is missing from a controlled list. What should I do?
faq_missing_term_answer: Contact the team, justifying the use of the term (publications, reference vocabularies). For mineralogy, the application relies on the Mindat vocabulary.
faq_service_account_purpose_title: What is a service account for?
faq_service_account_purpose_answer: A service account lets an application, not a person, use the API: for example collection management software, a LIMS or an automatic declaration script. It is attached to an individual, so that someone carries the responsibility for the actions made through the API.
faq_service_account_difference_title: How is it different from a personal or generic account?
faq_service_account_difference_answer: A service account is reserved for exchanges between applications: it cannot sign in to the web interface. To work together in the interface, use a shared space instead, in which each member signs in with their own account (see “Can I share the management of my samples with other people?”). This way, each change stays attributed to its author.
faq_service_account_request_title: How do I request a service account?
faq_service_account_request_answer_1: Send your request through the contact form available from “profile”, “ask for a service account”, specifying:
faq_service_account_request_item_2: the space the account must be attached to;
faq_service_account_request_item_3: a person responsible for the account.
faq_service_account_request_answer_2: Once the request is accepted, you receive the API access credentials directly in your profile.
faq_service_account_responsibilities_ans: The designated responsible person answers for the use of the account. Keep the credentials in a safe place: do not share them, and never publish them, especially in a code repository. If they are compromised or the responsible person changes, let us know without delay so that the access can be revoked or reassigned. Samples declared by a service account must carry the usual information about their collectors and responsible parties.
